changelog: The system now checks its own update source at every start and every update check: if it was ever left pointing somewhere other than the official release -- which silently freezes a system on its old version -- it corrects itself and carries on updating.
details: 50b (bench revision, stacked on 50a for the next bare-number release): makes v13's rescue repair permanent on the main line. A unit whose CYTECH_MANIFEST_URL is not the canonical main one cannot update at all, and neither failure looks like a failure. The retired test branch leaves it on whatever version that branch serves, reporting 'up to date' -- truthfully, relative to that frozen source -- forever. Any other ref (a release tag left behind by a service visit, a commit SHA, or no ref at all) makes cytech_update.sh build a download base that 404s, so the owner sees 'Update failed while downloading <file>. Will retry on next boot.', which never resolves. v13 (published on the test branch) reached the frozen class by rewriting the URL during Check for Update and at boot; this revision puts the same repair in first_boot.sh and cytech_check_only.sh on main, so it reaches every unit that ever gets these scripts -- including ones sealed in their box, since the boot call sits above the .zero_touch_completed branch and runs before anything reads the URL. Scope is deliberately narrow: it rewrites the URL only when the host is raw.githubusercontent.com, the repo path is exactly slychiu/ComfortHA-yaml, and the ref is something other than main (test, a tag, a SHA, or missing). A local test mirror, another repo, a nested path, a foreign host or a non-manifest path is left strictly alone -- verified by the unit suite, which also covers the surrounding shapes, a quoted value, a trailing CR, a commented-out line, an already-correct file (silent no-op, no backup) and a missing file (fresh unit, no crash). The original value is kept once in /config/.cytech_secrets.bak_pre_manifest_repair and never overwritten; a unit that already carries the v13 rescue's backup keeps it, and this line writes its own. The in-process variable is refreshed, so the very press that repairs the URL already checks against the real latest rather than waiting for the next pass. cytech_update.sh is re-shipped unchanged in the same payload: on a unit healed by the v12/v13 rescue it is still the old pre-v42-era updater, which has no tag-scoped downloads and no Core-restart triggers, so shipping the current one is what converges those units onto the fleet updater. No new entity, no dashboard change, no owner-visible screen.
